items.title: Does this commit reach production?
items.description: Flip each gate between pass and fail. The output shows whether the same commit should reach production and where the pipeline should stop.
items.compute: const buildOk = params.buildPasses >= 1; const testsOk = params.testsPass >= 1; const bypass = params.continueOnError >= 1; const stagingOk = params.stagingPasses >= 1; let reachesProduction = 0; let stoppedStage = 0; if (!buildOk) { stoppedStage = 1; } else if (!testsOk && !bypass) { stoppedStage = 2; } else if (!stagingOk) { stoppedStage = 3; } else { reachesProduction = 1; stoppedStage = 4; } return { reachesProduction, stoppedStage };

outputs.label: Stop point (1 build, 2 test, 3 staging, 4 production)

items.title: How much does an unrehearsed rollback path actually cost?
items.description: A rollback path that's designed and rehearsed in advance takes minutes. One improvised for the first time during an active incident — figuring out which previous version to put back into production, whether the rollback script even still works — routinely takes far longer, while broken code keeps serving every user who requests it. Drag the slider to see how much that gap in rollback speed actually costs in affected requests.

params.name: usersAffectedPerMinute
params.label: Users hitting the broken deploy per minute

items.compute: const usersAffected = params.minutesToRollback * params.usersAffectedPerMinute; return { usersAffected };

outputs.label: Users who hit the broken deploy before rollback completes
